html:
SMTO-EXE-0068 — The clipboard tools on the Gateway computer aren't working

GUID: 9f01a0c0-3c94-5db4-b637-52f723ac038c
Slug: clipboard-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO reached the Gateway computer, but the program it uses there to copy and paste is missing or stopped working. The copy or paste didn't finish.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway to make sure its clipboard helper is installed. On Linux that is xclip, or wl-clipboard on Wayland desktops. SMTO doesn't install these helpers by itself, and without them it can't copy or paste on that computer.
  2. Have them restart the Gateway, then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for it. The Gateway checks for clipboard support when it starts, so a restart lets it find newly installed tools.
  3. Start a new task and, if SMTO was putting something on the clipboard, paste on that computer first to see what's there now. A new task sees the repaired clipboard, and checking first avoids copying the same thing twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads or sets the Gateway computer's clipboard and reports the result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway computer's operating system, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't include private clipboard contents in what you send.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The clipboard backend is unusable: readiness advertised no capabilities, a native utility or memory operation failed, or the clipboard worker or service raised an unexpected error before producing a result.

What this means

  • Clipboard readiness exposed no capabilities, an adapter or native memory operation failed, or a caught worker/service exception prevented a usable backend result. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Clipboard readiness exposed no capabilities, an adapter or native memory operation failed, or a caught worker/service exception prevented a usable backend result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect public backend readiness and the failing native/worker phase before checking dependencies or memory access.

How to fix it

  • Check the selected Gateway's clipboard readiness and prerequisites: Linux X11 needs xclip (a missing python-xlib or unreachable display is reported as no session instead); Wayland needs wl-copy/wl-paste and a reachable compositor socket; macOS needs the packaged PyObjC AppKit and Quartz bridges; Windows uses native Win32 APIs. Install only what readiness shows missing (nothing is installed automatically), restart the Gateway, refresh its capabilities, and check the Gateway log for clipboard worker failures.
  • Repair the indicated backend prerequisite or service failure on the selected Gateway; install dependencies only when readiness shows they are missing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Install the documented native prerequisites on the selected Gateway, then refresh Gateway capabilities.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended backend reports ready and returns a valid result for an explicit clipboard request.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
